title: There's a Volcano Three Times Taller Than Mount Everest

scenes.text: There's a volcano three times taller than Everest. You could stroll up it.
It's Olympus Mons, on Mars. It rises about 25 kilometres above the plains around it.
It's about 600 kilometres wide. Drop it on the United States and it would cover all of Arizona.
But its slopes are only a few degrees. Standing on it, you'd think you were on a flat plain. You couldn't even see the top.
It got so big because Mars has no moving plates. On Earth, the crust drifts over hot spots and spreads lava into island chains. On Mars, it piled up in one place for billions of years.
Weaker gravity helps too, so a mountain can grow taller before it sags. Would you hike a volcano the size of a state?

description:
There's a volcano three times taller than Mount Everest, and you could walk up it.
Olympus Mons on Mars rises about 25 km above the surrounding plains and is roughly 600 km across, about the size of Arizona. Its slopes are only a few degrees, so it would feel like a gently sloping plain. It grew so large because Mars has no plate tectonics to move the crust away from the hot spot, and its lower gravity lets mountains grow taller.
Would you hike a volcano the size of a country?
